name: UPSC / Civil Services
description: Civil Services (Prelims) style questions: Indian polity, modern history, geography, economy and environment.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution can President's Rule be imposed in a state?
questions.explanation: Article 356 provides for President's Rule on failure of constitutional machinery in a state. Article 352 is National Emergency, 360 is Financial Emergency.

questions.question: The Fundamental Rights are enshrined in which Part of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Part III (Articles 12–35) contains the Fundamental Rights. Part IV has the Directive Principles of State Policy.

questions.question: Who appoints the Chief Justice of India?
questions.explanation: The President appoints the CJI under Article 124, acting on the recommendation of the outgoing CJI / collegium (established by the Second and Third Judges Cases).

questions.question: A Money Bill can be introduced in the Lok Sabha only on the recommendation of whom?
questions.explanation: Under Article 117(1), a Money Bill requires the President's recommendation before introduction in the Lok Sabha, and it cannot originate in the Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976) is popularly known as what?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment, passed during the Emergency, altered the Preamble and dozens of provisions — hence the 'Mini Constitution' tag.

questions.question: The Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Part IV (Articles 36–51) lists the DPSPs, borrowed largely from the Irish Constitution. Part IVA has the Fundamental Duties.

questions.question: What is the term of a member of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: Rajya Sabha members serve 6-year terms, with one-third retiring every two years — the House is a permanent body.

questions.question: A National Emergency is proclaimed under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 352 deals with National Emergency (war, external aggression, armed rebellion). It has been proclaimed three times: 1962, 1971 and 1975.

questions.question: Who has the power to dissolve the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: The President can dissolve the Lok Sabha under Article 85, on the advice of the Council of Ministers. The Rajya Sabha cannot be dissolved.

questions.question: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act (1992) is related to which subject?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment constitutionalised Panchayati Raj (three-tier rural local government). The 74th Amendment covers urban Municipalities.

questions.question: In which year was the Battle of Plassey fought?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Plassey (23 June 1757) — Robert Clive's victory over Siraj-ud-Daulah — laid the foundation of British rule in India. Buxar followed in 1764.

questions.question: Who was the first Governor-General of independent India?
questions.explanation: Lord Mountbatten, the last Viceroy, became the first Governor-General of independent India (Aug 1947 – June 1948). C. Rajagopalachari was the first Indian to hold the post.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi's Dandi March, marking the start of the Civil Disobedience Movement, took place in which year?
questions.explanation: The Salt March from Sabarmati to Dandi (12 March – 6 April 1930) launched the Civil Disobedience Movement against the salt tax.

questions.question: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in which year?
questions.explanation: On 13 April 1919 (Baisakhi), troops under General Dyer fired on an unarmed gathering at Amritsar — a turning point of the freedom struggle.

questions.question: On which date was the Constitution of India adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 (now Constitution Day) and came into force on 26 January 1950 (Republic Day).

questions.question: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the seven-member Drafting Committee set up on 29 August 1947.

questions.question: The Chauri Chaura incident (1922) led Mahatma Gandhi to withdraw which movement?
questions.explanation: After policemen were killed by a mob at Chauri Chaura (Feb 1922), Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement, insisting on non-violence.

questions.question: The Simla Agreement of 1972 was signed between India and which country?
questions.explanation: Signed by Indira Gandhi and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto after the 1971 war, the Simla Agreement committed both nations to resolving disputes bilaterally.

questions.question: The words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' were added to the Preamble by which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble during the Emergency.

questions.question: The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many Indian states?
questions.explanation: It passes through 8 states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.

questions.question: Which Indian mountain range is geologically older — the Himalayas or the Western Ghats?
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats (block mountains, formed during Gondwana breakup) are far older than the young fold mountains of the Himalayas.

questions.question: Which river is historically known as the 'Sorrow of Bengal'?
questions.explanation: The Damodar's devastating floods earned it the name 'Sorrow of Bengal'; the DVC project later tamed it. The Kosi is the 'Sorrow of Bihar'.

questions.question: The southwest monsoon normally arrives over the Kerala coast around which time?
questions.explanation: The monsoon 'onset' over Kerala is around 1 June (normal date), progressing northward to cover the country by mid-July.

questions.question: In which year was the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) established?
questions.explanation: The RBI began operations on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act 1934 (Hilton Young Commission's recommendation). It was nationalised in 1949.

questions.question: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) came into force across India on which date?
questions.explanation: GST — 'One Nation, One Tax' — was launched at midnight on 1 July 2017, via the 101st Constitutional Amendment.

questions.question: The Ramsar Convention (1971) is related to the conservation of what?
questions.explanation: The Ramsar Convention is an international treaty for the conservation and wise use of wetlands; India has 80+ Ramsar sites.

questions.question: In which year was Project Tiger launched in India?
questions.explanation: Project Tiger was launched on 1 April 1973 from Jim Corbett National Park; India hosts ~70% of the world's wild tigers.

questions.question: India's first nuclear test, code-named 'Smiling Buddha', was conducted in which year?
questions.explanation: 'Smiling Buddha' was a peaceful nuclear explosion at Pokhran on 18 May 1974. Pokhran-II followed in 1998.

questions.question: Which constitutional body conducts the Civil Services Examination (IAS/IPS)?
questions.explanation: The Union Public Service Commission (Articles 315–323) conducts the CSE for the IAS, IPS, IFS and other All-India Services.

questions.question: The National Emergency declared on 25 June 1975 was proclaimed during the prime ministership of whom?
questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi's government declared the 21-month Emergency citing 'internal disturbance' — the only Emergency on that ground.
